### Primaquine regimens by G6PD status

| G6PD category | Radical-cure treatment policy | Treatment implementation | Follow-up approach | Follow-up implementation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **G6PD normal male: ? 4 IU/g Hb, G6PD normal female: ? 6 U/g Hb** | PQ 1.0 mg/kg/day over 7 days | Not implemented | DOT by health centre or VMW at patients' home | Implemented |
| **G6PD intermediate females: 4.1-6.0 IU/g Hb** | PQ 0.75 mg/kg/week weekly for 8 weeks | Implemented | DOT by health centre or VMW at patients' home, testing of Hb level on D0, 3, and 7 | Implemented |
| **G6PD deficient: ? 4 IU/g Hb** | PQ 0.75 mg/kg/week weekly for 8 weeks | Implemented | DOT by health centre or VMW at patients' home, testing of Hb level on D0, 3, and 7 | Implemented |

### Country-specific policy context

<div class="country-policy-context">Changed to 7-day PQ in 2023; Follow-up days changed 2023 when there was a switch from 14 day PQ to low dose 7-day PQ.  Before the switch to high-dose 7 day, VMW follow up was conducted at patients home checking for adherence and side effects, and partially implemented due to feasibility considerations. It also included DOT according to guidelines was not implemented as DOT; Tafenoquine is included  the 2025 update but needs country regulatory approval; Quinine can be used as second line if AL is not available for malaria in first trimester of pregnancy.</div>
